summary.short: Chile's Law 21.459 creates criminal offences for attacks on computer systems and data, illicit access and interception, computer forgery and fraud, and abuse of devices; it repeals Law 19.223 and amends procedural and other laws to align with the Budapest Convention, including data preservation duties for service providers.
summary.long: Law 21.459 defines computer offences in Title I, covering attacks on system integrity (Art. 1), illicit access (Art. 2), interception (Art. 3), data integrity (Art. 4), computer forgery (Art. 5), receiving illicitly obtained data (Art. 6), computer fraud (Art. 7) and abuse of devices and programmes (Art. 8). Penalties are presidio menor prison terms and fines in monthly tax units. Art. 2 exempts certain security researchers who meet seven conditions, including registration with the National Cybersecurity Agency and prior notice to the Agency. Art. 10 sets aggravating circumstances (abuse of a position of trust, abuse of children or older adults, and disruption of public utilities or elections). Title II allows investigations to start by complaint of the Public Security Minister, permits judicial orders for special investigation techniques and undercover online agents (Art. 12), provides for forfeiture (Art. 13) and governs electronic investigation evidence (Art. 14). Art. 18 adds Criminal Procedure Code Art. 218 bis, under which providers must preserve data for 90 days, extendable once up to 180 days, and keep the request secret; it takes effect six months after a Transport Ministry regulation is published. Law 19.223 is repealed (Art. 17), and the General Telecommunications Law and the Corporate Criminal Liability Law 20.393 are amended. Arts. 19 and 21 take effect six months after publication. A transitional article applies the more favourable law to earlier acts.

relations.note: Art. 17 repeals Ley 19.223, subject to Transitory Art. 1 (facts committed before entry into force are judged under the law then in force, unless the new law is more favourable).
